cvEn:
Gracia (Yaffe) Harosh, daughter of Haya and Eliyahu, was born on the 12th of Iyar 5692 (18 May 1932) in the Old City of Jerusalem. The family home stood on Karaim Street. She completed elementary school and joined Hanoar Haoved, the working youth movement, and spent eight months in training at Kfar Hanoar Haoved in Ben Shemen. Her foreign given name was changed to "Yaffe," and it was under this name that people knew her: a cheerful, capable and kind-hearted girl.

For six months she served as a liaison in Gadna, the IDF youth battalions, and was then enlisted as a soldier among the defenders of the Old City of Jerusalem. She was stationed at the Warsaw position, and when that position fell to the enemy she moved to the Porat Yosef position, where she was killed on the 7th of Iyar 5708 (16 May 1948). As the attackers approached, she was about to throw a grenade at them when she was struck by a bullet, and the grenade exploded in her hand.

She was buried in the Old City of Jerusalem. Her name is inscribed on the memorial erected in the military cemetery on Mount Herzl in memory of the fallen of the Jewish Quarter and of the fighters who fell in the battle for Jerusalem and were buried on the Mount of Olives.
